chunks: And in the narration of Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abū Saʿīd al-Qammāṭ:
That Abū ʿAbdِ ٱللَّهِ عليه السلام was asked about someone who became junub at the beginning of the night in the Month of Ramadan, then slept until morning.
He said: “There is nothing upon him, and that is because his janābah occurred at a permissible time.”

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: entered the state of janabah (major ritual impurity)
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, during which fasting is observed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who becomes junub at night in Ramadan and sleeps until morning?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who enters the state of janabah during the night of Ramadan and then sleeps until morning. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no liability upon him, because the janabah took place during a time in which such an act was halal.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1897 - In the narration of Ibn Abi Nasr from Abu Sa'id al-Qammat:
Abu Abdullah (as) was asked about someone who became junub (in a state of ritual impurity) at the beginning of the night in the Month of Ramadan and then slept until morning.
Imam (as) said: "There is no penalty upon him, as his state of janabah occurred during a permissible time."
